about: Rover settings definition, owned by Trail_Tracer_Mower (docs/settings_def.json). The PC uses an unchanged copy. Words from the PC draft (Trail-Tracer-PC-Telemetry 22deeea); values checked against src/usb_msc_fat.cpp (defaults, limits) and src/main.cpp (STATIONARY_KEYS). Format: Trail-Tracer-PC-Telemetry docs/control_api.md, section 3. 'list' ends 'end <n> def 6'. Version 6: groups in user order ('groups'), a 'label' per setting, DSP settings (dsp_*) with read-only values in effect (dsp_*_eff, 'readonly': true; 'effect' names the _eff key of a setting). Version 7 (firmware 0.5.69): 'string' and 'choice' types, 'max_len', 'pattern' and 'dec'; the servo outputs by function (steer_*, throttle_*) replace PWM_OUT_n_*; drive_output, vehicle_name, steer_lpf_hz; CHARGE_MAX_SECONDS is the charge time. Version 8 (firmware 0.5.71): radio_mode (espnow or wifi, from the next start), read-only wifi_ssid and wifi_password (set or not set; USB 'wifi set' writes them). Version 9 (firmware 0.5.87): dsp_sweep_bins (off, auto or 1-8; the bins off that sweep 41.1-68.5 kHz; default auto).

vehicle_name.description: Vehicle name on the telemetry screen: letters, digits, space, _ and -; 16 at most
vehicle_name.label: Vehicle name

vehicleID.description: Vehicle number in the radio status text (V1.0 compatible); the telemetry screen shows the name
vehicleID.label: Vehicle number

drive_output.description: How the vehicle drives: servo = steering and throttle servos (as V1.0); can = motor controllers over CAN (mower); auto = can once a motor controller answers, else servo
drive_output.label: Drive output

battery_cells.description: Battery cells in series (2 for a 2S battery); the power graph scales from it
battery_cells.label: Battery cells

imu_required.description: No effect since firmware 0.5.40: with no working IMU, the gyro lock keeps the motors off (the main branch f10cd31). Kept for old config files
imu_required.label: Motion sensor required

usb_drive.label: USB drive for config.json
usb_drive.description: true (default): the rover shows config.json as a USB drive on the PC. false: no USB drive; change settings by command or in the telemetry program. Takes effect at the next start.

rx_channel.description: Transmitter channel that the Rx listens to
rx_channel.label: Wire channel

enable_sensor_2.description: On: the sensor board reads both sensors, and the rover shows and logs the sensor 2 data (position, radius, polarity, spectrum). Off: the board reads sensor 1 only and gives it all its processing time, for the best sensor 1 signal. Sensor 2 always listens on Tx channel 1. Sensor 2 data changes no rover behaviour unless Use sensor 2 for control is also on
enable_sensor_2.label: Sensor 2

CRUISE_THROTTLE.description: Throttle pulse when the vehicle follows the wire
CRUISE_THROTTLE.label: Cruise throttle

CREEP_THROTTLE.description: Throttle pulse for the slow approach
CREEP_THROTTLE.label: Slow throttle

kp.description: Proportional part of the steering PID
kp.label: Steering gain (P)

ki.description: Integral part of the steering PID
ki.label: Steering gain (I)

kd.description: Derivative part of the steering PID
kd.label: Steering gain (D)

steer_lpf_hz.description: Low-pass filter on the steering PID output (2nd order), against jitter from the D term. 0 = off
steer_lpf_hz.label: Steering output filter

steering_rate_kp.description: Proportional part of the yaw-rate steering PID (gyro feedback; output -1..1)
steering_rate_kp.label: Gyro steering gain (P)

steering_rate_ki.description: Integral part of the yaw-rate steering PID
steering_rate_ki.label: Gyro steering gain (I)

steering_rate_kd.description: Derivative part of the yaw-rate steering PID
steering_rate_kd.label: Gyro steering gain (D)

steering_rate_pid_direction.description: Yaw-rate PID direction: true reverses it
steering_rate_pid_direction.label: Reverse gyro steering

steering_rate_max_dps.description: Yaw rate in deg/s at full steering command
steering_rate_max_dps.label: Turn rate at full steer

BTxCreepDuration.description: Time of the slow approach after a beacon
BTxCreepDuration.label: Slow approach time

stuck_threshold_mm.description: Smallest movement that counts as not stuck
stuck_threshold_mm.label: Stuck: smallest movement

stuck_timeout_ms.description: Time below that movement before the vehicle is stuck
stuck_timeout_ms.label: Stuck: time

SineSwerveAmplitude.description: Swerve size to each side (0 = off)
SineSwerveAmplitude.label: Swerve size

CHARGE_VBATT_STOP.description: End the charge at this battery voltage. STM32 limit 16.0 V
CHARGE_VBATT_STOP.label: Charge end voltage

CHARGE_MAX_CURRENT.description: Stop the charge above this current, then wait 10 s. STM32 limit 6.0 A
CHARGE_MAX_CURRENT.label: Charge current limit

CHARGE_MAX_SECONDS.description: Longest charge: the sensor board stops a charge after this time
CHARGE_MAX_SECONDS.label: Charge time limit

rover_mode.description: What drive mode 2 (autonomous) runs. rover: the full mission (roam, turn back at the wire, return, join, follow, dock, depart), in the Roam mode below. follow only: find the wire, join it, follow it. position follower (expert): the plain position-steering wire follower, which circles when it starts off the wire. Cruise mode (RC throttle) always uses the wire follower
rover_mode.label: Autonomous mode

rover_goal_cw.description: Every roam mode: the goal direction along the wire, into the charger: on = clockwise seen from above
rover_goal_cw.label: Charger direction clockwise

rover_sensor_height_mm.description: Every roam mode: the height of the sensor centre above the wire
rover_sensor_height_mm.label: Sensor height

rover_seek_vbatt.description: Every roam mode: return to the wire below this battery voltage (filtered). 0 = off
rover_seek_vbatt.label: Return battery voltage

rover_entry_btx.description: Every roam mode: the beacon channel before the charger: slow approach (0 = none)
rover_entry_btx.label: Beacon before the charger

rover_exit_btx.description: Every roam mode: the beacon channel after the charger exit: the vehicle turns back if it meets this beacon first (0 = none)
rover_exit_btx.label: Beacon after the charger

rover_lost_timeout_s.description: Every roam mode: the rover stops after this long without the wire in a join, a follow or a depart (0 = never)
rover_lost_timeout_s.label: Stop after wire lost for

espnow_enabled.description: Telemetry messages over ESP-NOW. If telemetry_enabled is also false, the vehicle takes no commands. The vehicle refuses false over ESP-NOW
espnow_enabled.label: Radio messages

telemetry_rate_hz.description: Vehicle log sample rate in Hz. Below 100 Hz an anti-alias filter (two moving averages) runs first. Other values go to the nearest allowed rate
telemetry_rate_hz.label: Log rate

telemetry_bins_hz.description: Rate in Hz of the coil magnitudes of all 8 frequency bins in the vehicle log, for the per-bin plots. The same anti-alias filter as the log rate runs first. 0 = off
telemetry_bins_hz.label: Coil plot rate

espnow_tx_power_dbm.description: Radio transmit power in dBm, 0.25 dB steps. 19.5 is the radio's maximum. A low power over the radio can lose the link to this vehicle
espnow_tx_power_dbm.label: Radio power

telemetry_enabled.description: Vehicle log over ESP-NOW. If espnow_enabled is also false, the vehicle takes no commands. The vehicle refuses false over ESP-NOW
telemetry_enabled.label: Telemetry

radio_mode.label: Radio link
radio_mode.description: How the vehicle sends its telemetry. espnow: straight to a monitor, with no network. wifi: through a Wi-Fi network to the PC telemetry server; the vehicle then takes no commands over the radio. A change takes effect after a save and a restart. The vehicle refuses wifi over ESP-NOW.

wifi_ssid.label: Wi-Fi network
wifi_ssid.description: The network name for radio_mode wifi. Set it over USB with: wifi set <network> <password>. The vehicle keeps it in its own memory, not in config.json.

wifi_password.label: Wi-Fi password
wifi_password.description: Shows set or not set. The vehicle never shows or sends the password. Set it over USB with the wifi set command.

cmd_key.description: Fleet password; 0 = blank (accepts key 0); USB or config.json only
cmd_key.label: Fleet password

dsp_frame_period_us.label: Update period
dsp_frame_period_us.description: Time between two position updates from the sensor board. A longer period averages more signal: less noise, slower response. The board uses the nearest period that it can make. Default 10000 us (10 ms). The sensor board runs set steps: 2354, 2938, 3522 ... us (+584 us a step) with the slow ADC on, 2336, 2628 ... us (+292 us) with it off; a setting runs at the step at or below it. The shortest setting is 2938 us with every link, so the sensor board keeps spare time; the board refuses a shorter one. Below 5000 us the CPU load can pass the 70 % target with Wi-Fi.

dsp_frame_period_us_eff.label: Update period (in effect)
dsp_frame_period_us_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_sensors_eff.label: Sensors on the board (in effect)
dsp_sensors_eff.description: The number of sensors the sensor board reads now (its answer): 2 with the setting Sensor 2 on, 1 with it off. Empty until the board answers.

dsp_bin_hz_0.label: Frequency slot 1
dsp_bin_hz_0.description: Frequency that slot 1 listens to, in Hz; 0 = slot off. Default: transmitter channel 1 (53333.3 Hz). Slots 1-5 are the transmitter channels 1-5.

dsp_bin_hz_0_eff.label: Frequency slot 1 (in effect)
dsp_bin_hz_0_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_bin_hz_1.label: Frequency slot 2
dsp_bin_hz_1.description: Frequency that slot 2 listens to, in Hz; 0 = slot off. Default: transmitter channel 2 (55315.5 Hz). Slots 1-5 are the transmitter channels 1-5.

dsp_bin_hz_1_eff.label: Frequency slot 2 (in effect)
dsp_bin_hz_1_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_bin_hz_4.label: Frequency slot 5

dsp_bin_hz_4_eff.label: Frequency slot 5 (in effect)
dsp_bin_hz_4_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_bin_hz_5_eff.label: Frequency slot 6 (in effect)

dsp_slow_adc.label: Battery and charge measurement

dsp_pga_eff.label: Input gain (in effect)
dsp_pga_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_sweep_bins.label: Sweep bins
dsp_sweep_bins.description: Bins that are off (frequency 0) step across 41.1-68.5 kHz for the spectrum view: auto = all free bins (default), 1-8 = that many, off = no sweep. The PC sets the range. Rx STM32 2.0.51 or later.

dsp_lanes_eff.label: Sensor lanes (in effect)
dsp_lanes_eff.description: The sensor of each data lane on the sensor board now (its answer): 2 = lane 1 sensor 1, lane 2 sensor 2 (Sensor 2 on); 0 = sensor 1 only (Sensor 2 off). Empty until the board answers.

dsp_xy_mask.label: Position slots (bit mask)
dsp_xy_mask.description: Slots that give x/y positions in place of signal strengths: bit 0 = slot 1, bit 1 = slot 2, ... bit 7 = slot 8. 0 (default) = none.

dsp_xy_mask_eff.label: Position slots (bit mask) (in effect)

throttle_min_us.label: Throttle end, low

throttle_max_us.description: Throttle end point, high pulse (full forward)
throttle_max_us.label: Throttle end, high

dt_channels.description: 255 = auto: every Tx channel with a position bin within 30 Hz of its carrier. Else a mask: 1 = CH1, 2 = CH2, 4 = CH3, 8 = CH4, 16 = CH5 (add them; 31 = all five); 0 = polarity detection off. Rx STM32 2.1.134+

dt_side_a_ch1.label: Side A of Tx channel 1

tx_dir_ch1.description: The way positive Tx current runs round the loop, seen from above: 0 = not set (no inside/outside), 1 = clockwise (default), 2 = counterclockwise. Wrong: the rover faults at the start in rover mode (polarity says outside); then set the other way.

steer_frame.description: vehicle: x as the sensor sees it. world: x signed by the heading round the loop, so a vehicle on the wire the wrong way turns round. World needs polarity (Rx STM32 2.2.0+) and the current direction of the followed Tx channel; without them: vehicle.

rover_join_no_pol.description: Bounce and Reverse bounce: with no polarity at a join: inside = assume the rover is inside the loop; stop = stop. Join then leave always assumes inside at the start and takes the side from polarity when it has it
rover_join_no_pol.label: Join without polarity

rover_roam_speed_mps.description: Every roam mode: the one top speed: the vehicle speed at full drive command; roam drives at it
rover_roam_speed_mps.label: Roam speed

rover_bounce_m.description: Bounce and Reverse bounce: the distance to the wire at which the rover stops and turns back into the loop
rover_bounce_m.label: Bounce distance

rover_bounce_spread_deg.description: Every roam mode: a random angle from minus to plus this value is added to each planned depart angle (Bounce and Reverse bounce: the mirror of the measured wire angle at a bounce, and the depart angle target at the end of a follow; Join then leave: the depart angle target). 0 = always the planned angle. A wider spread covers the lawn more evenly; a narrow spread can repeat the same paths. A depart past a limit takes that limit
rover_bounce_spread_deg.label: Depart angle spread

rover_bounce_min_deg.description: Every roam mode: the least angle between the wire and the depart heading; the most is 180 deg minus it. A planned angle outside the limits takes the nearer limit. It keeps the rover off a shallow path along the wire, and it must exceed the uncertainty of the measured wire angle
rover_bounce_min_deg.label: Depart angle limit

rover_rearm_drop_m.description: Every roam mode: outside the loop (polarity), the rover turns round again each time its distance from the wire grows this much since the last turn-back
rover_rearm_drop_m.label: Turn-back repeat distance

rover_beacon_bounce.description: Every roam mode: in roam and return, turn round at a beacon
rover_beacon_bounce.label: Turn round at a beacon

rover_beacon_m.description: Every roam mode: the beacon distance at which the rover stops and turns round
rover_beacon_m.label: Beacon turn distance

rover_beacon_rearm_m.description: Every roam mode: after a beacon turn, the beacon counts again past this distance
rover_beacon_rearm_m.label: Beacon re-arm distance

rover_beacon_spread_deg.description: Every roam mode: a random angle from minus to plus this value on the 180 deg beacon turn
rover_beacon_spread_deg.label: Beacon turn spread

rover_approach_m.description: Every roam mode. Join then leave: the join point lies inside this distance to the wire (with the re-arm radius fall), for a turn at the wire and for a return. Bounce and Reverse bounce: inside it the rover drives at the approach speed, and a Bounce return starts its join here
rover_approach_m.label: Approach distance

rover_approach_pct.description: Every roam mode: percent of the roam speed. Join then leave: the join, the short follow and the depart arc. Bounce and Reverse bounce: inside the approach distance and the join. Every mode: the probe and the drive outside the loop
rover_approach_pct.label: Approach speed

rover_join_angle_deg.description: Join then leave, and the follow of a Reverse bounce return: the most angle between the heading and the wire as the follow closes on its line; the rover never drives square-on at the wire, where the field has its null. Turn radius 0: also the join heading. Every roam mode: near the wire on a square-on approach, the square-on guard turns the rover onto this angle (a turn of 90 deg minus this value). 45 deg nominal. The Bounce mode join drives straight to the wire and turns on the spot
rover_join_angle_deg.label: Approach angle

rover_wrong_dir_check.description: Every roam mode, in the follow after a start on the wire and after a charge; the Bounce mode also in every other follow. Polarity direction against the goal direction, or the exit beacon before the entry beacon: turn round
rover_wrong_dir_check.label: Wrong-direction check

rover_depart_min_m.description: Every roam mode: after a charge, follow a random distance from minimum to maximum (equal: fixed), then turn to the depart angle
rover_depart_min_m.label: Depart distance minimum

rover_depart_max_m.description: Every roam mode: after a charge, follow a random distance from minimum to maximum (equal: fixed), then turn to the depart angle
rover_depart_max_m.label: Depart distance maximum

rover_probe_m.description: Every roam mode: at a start in range, a straight drive of this length, forward when the wire is further away, else reverse; it gives the heading to the wire (0 = no probe)
rover_probe_m.label: Probe length

rover_imu_roll.description: Every roam mode: turn the Rx x and y back by the accelerometer roll before the heading fit, so a side slope does not bend the lateral wire offset. inverted: the IMU sits the other way round (check on a side slope over the wire)
rover_imu_roll.label: IMU roll correction

rover_no_tx_roam_s.description: Every roam mode, in roam and return: no Tx signal (the wire signal under 10 dB on both sensors) this long: stop and wait until it returns. Far from the wire in a large loop the signal can drop out
rover_no_tx_roam_s.label: Roam: stop after no Tx signal for

rover_no_tx_s.description: Every roam mode, in join, follow, depart and dock: no Tx signal (the wire signal under 10 dB on both sensors) this long: stop and wait until it returns
rover_no_tx_s.label: Stop after no Tx signal for

rover_roam_time_s.description: Every roam mode: roam this long, then find the wire, join it and follow it for the follow time; then depart at the depart angle and roam again. The time counts only in roam (not while it waits for the Tx signal). A charge return comes first; after a charge both times start again. 0 = off (also when the follow time is 0)
rover_roam_time_s.label: Roam time

rover_follow_time_s.description: Every roam mode: after the roam time, follow the wire this long, then depart at the depart angle and roam again. A charge return comes first. 0 = off (also when the roam time is 0)
rover_follow_time_s.label: Follow time

rover_follow_exit_deg.description: Every roam mode: the planned angle between the wire and the depart heading, before the spread and the limits. Join then leave: each depart. Bounce and Reverse bounce: the end of a timed follow and the depart after a charge (a bounce mirrors the measured wire angle). 90 = straight into the loop
rover_follow_exit_deg.label: Depart angle target

rover_rearm_fall_mm.description: Every roam mode: after any turn, the next turn at the wire (Join then leave: the join point) arms when the wire radius falls this much below its highest value since the turn: the rover closes on the wire again. Join then leave: the side reading must fall the same amount. 30 mm is 3 x the radius noise. More delays the turn; less lets noise arm it
rover_rearm_fall_mm.label: Re-arm radius fall

wire_max_depth_mm.description: Every roam mode: the most the wire lies deeper than the sensor height setting, anywhere round the loop. The inside/outside value changes side only when the sensor comes this near the wire: deeper wire is seen farther out. 120 mm takes a wire buried 120 mm deeper than the setting. Too small: a real crossing at deep wire shows late; too large: a false polarity reading near the wire can change the side
wire_max_depth_mm.label: Wire extra depth, maximum

use_sensor_2.description: On (with Sensor 2 on): the inside/outside value, the heading round the loop and the follow direction come from the sensor nearest the wire; Join then leave and Reverse bounce: sensor 2 leads when the rover drives in reverse. Off: sensor 2 is data only (log and app), and every rover decision uses sensor 1. Turn it on only when sensor 2 faces the same way as sensor 1 and has the same sign: a sensor 2 with the opposite sign gives the wrong side
use_sensor_2.label: Use sensor 2 for control

rover_bounce_style.description: How the rover turns back at the wire. Bounce: as it drives, the rover measures the distance and the direction of the wire; at the bounce distance it stops, turns on the spot and drives back into the loop at the mirror angle. Join then leave: the rover joins the wire on a sweeping turn, follows it for the short follow time, then leaves on an arc back into the loop. Reverse bounce: as Bounce, but the rover does not turn on the spot: it stops, drives the other way and sweeps round to the mirror angle (with Use sensor 2 for control on, sensor 2 at the back leads in reverse). Join then leave and Reverse bounce never turn tighter than the turn radius
rover_bounce_style.label: Roam mode

rover_follow_inset_m.description: Every roam mode: the follow holds this far inside the wire. 0: the follow runs over the wire (a follow offset breaks the charge station entry)
rover_follow_inset_m.label: Follow inset

rover_bounce_follow_s.description: Join then leave only: the short follow lasts this long from the moment the rover reaches the follow line; it brings the heading parallel to the wire before the depart. 3 s in the simulation
rover_bounce_follow_s.label: Short follow time

rover_turn_radius_m.description: Join then leave and Reverse bounce: the tightest turn the rover drives, as the radius of its turn. A larger radius slips the wheels less and spares the lawn. 0: the rover turns on the spot
rover_turn_radius_m.label: Turn radius

rover_sonar_mm.description: Bounce and Reverse bounce, in the roam drive only: when sonar 1 or 2 (front) reads under this distance for the readings in a row, Bounce stops and turns 180 deg and Reverse bounce stops and drives the other way; in Reverse bounce sonar 3 or 4 (back) does the same while the rover drives backward. It keeps the rover off objects on the lawn. Higher: the rover turns farther from an object, also at objects it would pass. Lower: the rover comes closer before it turns, and the stop can take it into the object. A reading of 0 (no echo) never counts. 0 = sonar off. The unit is the Nano's (mm)
rover_sonar_mm.label: Sonar trigger distance

rover_sonar_count.description: Bounce and Reverse bounce: the number of sonar records in a row under the sonar trigger distance before the rover acts. One reading at or over the distance, or of 0, starts the count again. It stops one false echo (grass, a bump) from turning the rover. Higher: fewer false turns, but the rover drives on for longer before it turns (one record more each Nano period). Lower: a faster turn, more false turns
rover_sonar_count.label: Sonar readings in a row

usb_heartbeat.description: On: the vehicle prints the HB line on USB once a second (time, Rx packets, control passes, drive mode, memory, CPU load). The bench tools read it, and it keeps an idle USB link busy (an idle ESP32-S2 USB link can stop). Off (default): a quiet USB console for the user; the line then prints only after the USB command 'verbose on' (this start only). The monitor role prints its own 1 s line in any case
usb_heartbeat.label: USB heartbeat
